headline: BRTA: Front number plates mandatory for motorcycles by Nov 15
summary: Motorcycle and scooter owners must install front registration plates at their own expense by the deadline.
details: The Bangladesh Road Transport Authority (BRTA) has introduced new rules requiring all motorcycle and scooter owners to install number plates at the front of their vehicles by November 15.
Until now, motorcycles were only required to have retro-reflective rear number plates equipped with radio-frequency identification (RFID) tags.
Under the new directive, front plates must be conventional number plates rather than RFID-equipped ones, and they must be fitted at the owners' expense.
For scooters, the front plates must be made of stainless steel or aluminium, measuring 285mm in length and 50mm in width.
These plates must feature a white background with registration numbers displayed in black Bangla letters and numerals.
For other motorcycles, the front plates must also measure 285mm by 50mm, with letters and numerals at least 20mm high on all plates.
caption:
Motorcycle owners, take note: front number plates are now mandatory in Bangladesh.

The Bangladesh Road Transport Authority (BRTA) has introduced new rules requiring all motorcycle and scooter owners to install number plates at the front of their vehicles by November 15.

Until now, motorcycles were only required to have retro-reflective rear number plates equipped with radio-frequency identification (RFID) tags.

Under the new directive, front plates must be conventional number plates rather than RFID-equipped ones, and they must be fitted at the owners' expense.

For scooters, the front plates must be made of stainless steel or aluminium, measuring 285mm in length and 50mm in width.

These plates must feature a white background with registration numbers displayed in black Bangla letters and numerals.

For other motorcycles, the front plates must also measure 285mm by 50mm, with letters and numerals at least 20mm high on all plates.

Source: bdnews24.com, Dhaka Tribune, The Daily Star, Jamuna TV

headline: 1,186 deaths this year as measles outbreak claims 5 more lives in 24 hours
summary: The Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) reports a surge in measles cases and fatalities across Bangladesh.
details: Five people died within 24 hours (Thursday 8 AM to Friday 8 AM) with measles symptoms, according to a DGHS notice on Friday.
This brings the total number of deaths related to measles and its symptoms this year to 1,186.
Of these fatalities, 104 were confirmed cases of measles, while 1,082 died with measles-like symptoms.
In the last 24 hours alone, 1,210 new patients with measles symptoms were admitted to hospitals across the country.
Since March 15, a total of 187,615 patients with measles symptoms have been hospitalized.
Of those hospitalized, 180,002 patients have been discharged after receiving treatment.
The DGHS also reported that since March 15, there have been 211,040 suspected cases of measles in the country.
Out of these suspected cases, 22,972 have been confirmed as measles infections.
